queue_items.class: non-distinguishing construction offered as a binding ground
queue_items.claim: The row's second ground, the repeated wicked-genitive template, does not distinguish this pair from its immediate neighbourhood and carries no swept object or digit.
queue_items.grounds: The rationale states that זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים (oshb:Prov.15.8) and דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע (oshb:Prov.15.9) repeat a wicked-genitive template that supplies the construction ground binding the pair into one boundary decision. Re-derived from the bytes, that template binds nothing specific to this seam: the same construct-plus-wicked pattern stands two verses before the row's span at oshb:Prov.15.6, וּבִתְבוּאַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע (byte tier), and the two lexemes are ubiquitous - swept word-bound, the singular form stands in 36 verses and the plural in 35 verses book-wide - while word-bound the row's own two forms are different tokens (plural at 15:8, singular at 15:9), so the pair shares no wicked-token at that tier at all. No digit or swept object is named for the template anywhere in the row. This is not load-bearing: the primary hook is exemplary and verifies exactly as stated - the contiguous skeleton construction תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה / תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה stands in 11 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel: Prov.3.32, Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.15.9, Prov.15.26, Prov.16.5, Prov.17.15, Prov.20.10, Prov.20.23) and Prov.15.8|Prov.15.9 is the sole adjacent pair among them, the seam shares two word-bound tokens, and the accent claim is byte-true (יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Prov.15.8 carries ETNAHTA U+0591, so the phrase does close colon A there and open the line at 15:9). Both edges are clean by the word-bound metric: oshb:Prov.15.7|oshb:Prov.15.8 and oshb:Prov.15.9|oshb:Prov.15.10 each share no word-bound content token, as the neighbouring rows state.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): demote the wicked-genitive template from a binding construction ground to disclosed texture, naming its swept object and digit (word-bound, the singular wicked-token stands in 36 verses and the plural in 35 verses book-wide, and the same construct pattern stands at oshb:Prov.15.6 immediately outside the span), and leave the tocevat-YHWH hook as the row's single driver, which the sweep already sustains.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The construct phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.15.8) closes colon 1 of 15:8 (accent-verified: the ETNAHTA falls on its own final word), and the same phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.15.9) opens colon 1 at the head of 15:9 — a hook straddling the verse boundary, not a uniform 'opens the second colon' pattern in both lines; the phrase is one of 11 verses book-wide carrying this contiguous skeleton construction (sweep: 11 verses), and of those 11 this seam is the sole adjacent pair. The sacrifice-of-the-wicked construct זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים (oshb:Prov.15.8) and the way-of-the-wicked construct דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע (oshb:Prov.15.9) repeat the wicked-genitive template that supplies the construction ground binding the pair into one boundary decision.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading each verse as a separate single_proverb was the default starting point but was set aside once the repeated two-word phrase surfaced as a genuine consecutive catchword rather than a mere thematic echo.
observed_substrate_signals: exact construct phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.15.8) recurs as תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה at the head of oshb:Prov.15.9, a hook straddling the verse boundary, one of 11 verses book-wide carrying this phrase and this seam is the sole adjacent pair among those 11 (sweep: 11 verses)
both lines repeat the wicked-genitive construct template — זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים (oshb:Prov.15.8) and דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע (oshb:Prov.15.9) — alongside the shared tocevat-YHWH predicate
shipped_row.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism in both lines (sacrifice/prayer in 15:8, way/pursuer in 15:9); the repeated phrase is the cluster's driver, not the shared theme of divine displeasure by itself.

queue_items.class: byte-false adjacency claim defending the back seam
queue_items.claim: The row excludes the preceding verse's shared root on the stated ground that it is not adjacent to the chain, but that verse stands immediately before the chain's first verse.
queue_items.grounds: observed_substrate_signals[2] states that the report-noun at 15:30 shares the hearing root but is not adjacent to this chain and is excluded from it. Both sides of that seam, spliced at byte tier. Preceding row's closing verse, oshb:Prov.15.30: מְֽאוֹר עֵ֭ינַיִם יְשַׂמַּֽח לֵ֑ב שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה תְּדַשֶּׁן עָֽצֶם. This row's opening verse, oshb:Prov.15.31: אֹ֗זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת תּוֹכַ֣חַת חַיִּ֑ים בְּקֶ֖רֶב חֲכָמִ֣ים תָּלִֽין. Prov.15.30 is immediately adjacent to Prov.15.31, so the stated exclusion ground is false as written. The deciding object is word-bound content-token overlap, and by it the seam is empty: 15:30 carries שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה (byte tier) against 15:31's participle שֹׁ֭מַעַת (byte tier) - the same root in different word-bound tokens - and the two verses share no word-bound token at all, which is what actually holds the back edge. The preceding row states this correctly (a noun there against a participle here), so the boundary survives on grounds the corpus already carries; the defect is this row's own stated reason.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only, no span change): restate observed_substrate_signals[2] to exclude the 15:30 link on the true byte ground - oshb:Prov.15.30 stands immediately before the chain's first verse and shares the hearing root with it, but in a different word-bound token (שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה against שֹׁ֭מַעַת), so the seam carries no word-bound overlap and the root-level echo is disclosed as texture rather than as a chain link.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A two-link catchword chain binds these three verses: 15:31 and 15:32 both carry tokhachat, תּוֹכַ֣חַת (oshb:Prov.15.31) and תּ֝וֹכַ֗חַת (oshb:Prov.15.32), attached in both cases to a participle of the same root for hearing (שֹׁ֭מַעַת in 15:31, וְשׁוֹמֵ֥עַ in 15:32); then 15:32 and 15:33 both carry the noun musar, מ֭וּסָר (oshb:Prov.15.32) in the absolute state and מוּסַ֣ר (oshb:Prov.15.33) in the construct state 'discipline of wisdom' — the same lexeme linking the closing pair. The chapter's three sayings on receiving correction are stitched together by this overlapping pair of shared roots rather than by theme alone.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating each verse as its own single_proverb row was rejected: the tokhachat link (31-32) and the musar link (32-33) tie all three verses together as consecutive shared roots, not a merely thematic grouping.

queue_items.class: cluster warrant fails the corpus's own adjacent-seam metric
queue_items.claim: The pair's sole cohesion object is lexeme-level only - the seam shares no word-bound content token - which is the exact condition two rows earlier in this chapter give for refusing a multi-verse unit, and the row never states the book's default atomization rival.
queue_items.grounds: Re-derived from the bytes with the sweeps, object named first. The seam oshb:Prov.16.10|oshb:Prov.16.11 shares ZERO word-bound content tokens: 16:10 carries בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט (byte tier), whose word-bound skeleton stands in 4 verses book-wide (Prov.16.10, Prov.18.5, Prov.24.23, Prov.29.4), and 16:11 carries מִ֭שְׁפָּט (byte tier), whose word-bound skeleton stands in 12 verses book-wide (Prov.2.8, Prov.8.20, Prov.12.5, Prov.13.23, Prov.16.8, Prov.16.11, Prov.17.23, Prov.19.28, Prov.21.7, Prov.21.15, Prov.28.5, Prov.29.26) - two different word-bound objects. The apparent match is the contained-substring effect the toolkit hazard catalog warns about: a sweep of the 16:11 form returns 1 verse at byte tier but 13 at accent-stripped tier INCLUDING Prov.16.10, only because the prefixed form contains the bare one. The nearest word-bound match to 16:11's token is not 16:10 but מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Prov.16.8, two verses before this row's span. Both sides of the row's outer seams, spliced at byte tier, per the both-sides law: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.16.9: לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ ; the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.16.12: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא ; and the row's own two verses, oshb:Prov.16.10: קֶ֤סֶם עַֽל שִׂפְתֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל פִּֽיו ; oshb:Prov.16.11: פֶּ֤לֶס וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל אַבְנֵי כִֽיס. By the deciding object - word-bound content-token overlap - all 3 of the 3 seams touching this row (16:9|16:10, 16:10|16:11, 16:11|16:12) are empty, so nothing binds these two verses more tightly than either is bound to its outside neighbour. The rows spanning Prov.16.1 and Prov.16.9 refuse a multi-verse unit in this same chapter on precisely this test, stating that seams there share no word-bound token at all; this row builds a cluster at a seam of that description. Its strongest_rejected_alternative rejects only the wider royal-noun extension and never states the collection's default single_proverb atomization. Honest qualification: lexeme-level cohesion IS accepted elsewhere in the corpus - the row at Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 spans the seam 16:13|16:14, which is also word-bound empty (plural against singular) - but there the object recurs gap-free in 4 of 4 verses as a domain, whereas here it is a single lexeme in two verses that also stands bare two verses earlier.
queue_items.proposed_change: Proposal only, owner-triage input, applied to nothing: retire the proverb_cluster at Prov.16.10-Prov.16.11 and carry two single_proverb rows, Prov.16.10-Prov.16.10 and Prov.16.11-Prov.16.11 (full X-X span form), restoring the collection's ruled default. Both-sides resolution: because oshb:Prov.16.9|oshb:Prov.16.10 and oshb:Prov.16.11|oshb:Prov.16.12 are each word-bound empty, the retirement dissolves only the interior seam and disturbs neither outer boundary, and the row at Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 is untouched. If the adjudicator instead rules that lexeme-level adjacency governs (the standard the royal-noun run relies on at its 16:13|16:14 seam), the cluster stands but its rationale must be re-cut to name the object as a shared LEXEME in prefixed and bare forms rather than as a shared noun, to carry the book-wide digits above, and to state and reject the single_proverb atomization on byte grounds; the two remedies are mutually exclusive and the choice is the owner's, not this review's.

queue_items.class: mark tier mislabel and mark used for a function it cannot serve
queue_items.claim: The paseq is presented as a tier-3 corroborating signal for a verse-pair boundary; the tier belongs to a different layer and an intra-verse separator cannot corroborate that two verses cohere.
queue_items.grounds: The rationale states that both verses carry a paseq seg per the inventory (single-witness at each), a corroborating tier-3 signal rather than the boundary driver. The citation hygiene is right and the claim is inventory-true: pmarks_Prov.json records paseq at Prov.16.10 (1) and Prov.16.11 (1), the row makes no intra-verse position claim, and the single-witness qualifier is present. Two things are not right. First, the owner tier assignment of TIER-3 WEAK belongs to the parashah layer - the pmarks marks_note assigns it to petuchah and setumah in the Writings - while the paseq inventory carries no tier at all and is documented as count-only; importing the parashah tier onto the paseq layer is a tier conflation of the class the campaign forbids. Second, a paseq is an intra-verse separator: a paseq inside 16:10 and a separate paseq inside 16:11 carry no information about whether the two VERSES cohere, so the signal cannot corroborate this pairing in either direction. Not load-bearing on its own, since the row calls it corroboration rather than the driver.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): drop both the tier label and the corroboration function from the paseq sentence, or restate it as an untiered span-relevant disclosure - pmarks_Prov.json records one paseq seg at each of Prov.16.10 and Prov.16.11, count-only, single-witness, disclosed because the span touches them and bearing on nothing in the boundary decision.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry mishpat: בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט (oshb:Prov.16.10, 'in judgment') and מִ֭שְׁפָּט (oshb:Prov.16.11, 'a balance and scales of judgment') — a royal oracle that does not err in judgment is immediately followed by honest weights that belong to YHWH, two sayings on the standard of right judgment held together by the shared noun. Both verses also carry a paseq seg per the inventory (single-witness at each), a corroborating tier-3 signal rather than the boundary driver.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this pair forward to include 16:12-16:15 (the melekh/melakhim run) was considered but not adopted here: 16:11 itself carries no melekh token, so folding it into that run would claim continuity the bytes do not sustain; it is treated as its own mishpat-linked pair instead.

shipped_row.device_notes: Both lines are synthetic rather than antithetic; Prov.16.10 itself carries the royal-noun root מֶ֑לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.10), the same root anchoring the following run, but the pair's cohesion rests on the mishpat root shared by both verses — בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט (oshb:Prov.16.10) and מִ֭שְׁפָּט (oshb:Prov.16.11) — a tie the melekh/melakhim run at 16:12-16:15 cannot claim, since that run needs the royal-noun root present in 4 of 4 verses and 16:11 breaks that continuity; 16:10's incidental royal-noun overlap with the following run does not itself warrant redrawing either boundary.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A man's heart plans his course, but YHWH directs his steps; planning and outcome are opposed within the verse, echoing 16:1's opening contrast without being adjacent to it.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending a cluster back through 16:1 was considered and rejected on the same interior-incoherence audit as the bracket row at 16:1: across the 16:1-16:9 span (9 verses), word-bound content-token overlap between adjacent seams sits at most at the bare divine name, and 16:8|16:9, the seam immediately behind this verse, shares no word-bound token at all. 16:8's own divine-name gap (טוֹב מְ֭עַט בִּצְדָקָ֑ה מֵרֹ֥ב תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט, oshb:Prov.16.8) is noted as the same secondary texture disclosed at the bracket row.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Each of these 4 verses carries the royal noun: מְ֭לָכִים (oshb:Prov.16.12, plural 'kings'), מְ֭לָכִים (oshb:Prov.16.13, plural 'kings'), מֶ֥לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.14, singular 'king'), and מֶ֥לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.15, singular 'king') — a gap-free four-verse run naming kings (sweep: 4 of 4 verses), moving from kingship's abstract standard (wrongdoing as abomination, righteous lips as delight) to its concrete effect on a courtier's life (the king's wrath, the king's favor).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A wider six-verse 'kings run' proposed for 16:10-16:15 was tested and cut back: 16:11 carries zero instances of the melekh/melakhim root, so it is drafted with 16:10 as its own mishpat-linked pair instead, and this row is bounded to the 4-verse span where the royal noun recurs verse by verse. Prov.16.10 independently carries מֶ֑לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.10), the identical royal-noun root shared by 4 of 4 verses in the following run (16:12-16:15), so its absence from this row's span does not reflect a root-absence claim but rather that 16:10 is engaged elsewhere, bound forward to 16:11 by the shared mishpat root (בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט, oshb:Prov.16.10; מִ֭שְׁפָּט, oshb:Prov.16.11) instead.

queue_items.claim: The chiasm is described with two byte-false positional claims: neither second-colon body-part form closes its verse.
queue_items.grounds: Spliced byte-tier from the staged verse map, Prov.18.6 reads שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא and Prov.18.7 reads פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ; each is seven words with the etnahta on word 4 (בְרִ֑יב and ל֑וֹ), so the second colon is words 5-7 in both. The row states that Prov.18.6 closes וּ֝פִ֗יו and that Prov.18.7 closes וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו, but those forms are word 5 of 7 and OPEN the second colon: Prov.18.6 closes on יִקְרָֽא and Prov.18.7 closes on נַפְשֽׁוֹ. The device survives the correction and is in fact stronger than the row states - the head noun is byte-identical in both verses, כְ֭סִיל standing at word 2 of each, and the body-part terms do reverse across the pair (שִׂפְתֵ֣י ... וּ֝פִ֗יו against פִּֽי ... וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו) - so this is a defective positional description inside a sound warrant, not a failed warrant. Both sides of both seams check clean at word-bound skeleton tier: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.18.5, שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.18.6, and the row's closing verse Prov.18.7 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.18.8, דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן.
